p.i: Mormon’s second letter to his son Moroni.

chapter.li: LEChapter9 Verse1 My dear son, I’m writing to 2PSF you again, so 2PSF you know I’m still alive, but I’m writing about serious and upsetting matters. VerseEnd Verse2 I’ve had a severe battle with the Lamanites from which we didn’t emerge victorious. Archeantus has died by the sword, as well as Luram and Emron; indeed, we’ve lost a large number of our best men. VerseEnd Verse3 And now, my son, I’m afraid the Lamanites will destroy this people since they don’t repent. And Satan is continually stirring them up to be angry with each other. VerseEnd Verse4 So I’m working with them constantly. When I speak God’s word with sharpness, they’re offended and grow angry with me. When I don’t use any sharpness, they harden their hearts against it. I’m afraid the Spirit of the Lord has stopped struggling with them. VerseEnd Verse5 Indeed, they become so incredibly angry that it seems to me they aren’t even afraid of death. They’ve lost their love for each other and constantly thirst for blood and revenge. VerseEnd Verse6 Now, my dear son, despite their hardness, let’s work diligently, because if we were to stop working, we would come under condemnation. We have a labor to perform while we inhabit our mortal bodies, so we can overcome the enemy of all righteousness and rest our souls in God’s kingdom. VerseEnd

Verse7 Now I’ll write a little about this people’s suffering. According to the intelligence I’ve received from Amoron, the Lamanites have many prisoners that they took from the tower of Sherrizah — and there were men, women, and children. VerseEnd Verse8 They’ve killed the husbands and fathers of those women and children. And they feed the women with their husbands’ flesh, and the children with their fathers’ flesh. And they only give them a little water. VerseEnd Verse9 Despite this great abomination of the Lamanites, it doesn’t exceed that of our people in Moriantum. There they took many Lamanite young women prisoner. After depriving them of what was most dear and precious above all things — chastity and virtue — VerseEnd Verse10 they murdered them in a most cruel manner, torturing their bodies until they died. After they’ve done this, they devour their flesh like wild animals because of their hard hearts, and they do it as a sign of bravery. VerseEnd Verse11 My dear son, how can a people like this, who are uncivilized — VerseEnd Verse12 and only a few years ago they were a civil and delightful people — VerseEnd Verse13 how can a people like this, who take pleasure in so much abomination, VerseEnd Verse14 how can we expect God to hold back His hand in judgment against us? VerseEnd Verse15 My heart cries out: Woe to this people! O God, bring down 2PSI Your judgment, and hide their sins, wickedness, and abominations from 2PSI Your face! VerseEnd

Verse16 Also, my son, there are many widows and their daughters who remain in Sherrizah. And that part of the supplies the Lamanites didn’t take, Zenephi’s army has taken, leaving them to wander wherever they can looking for food. Many old women faint as they go and die. VerseEnd Verse17 The army that’s with me is weak. The Lamanite armies are between me and Sherrizah. All those who have fled to Aaron’s army have fallen victim to their awful brutality. VerseEnd Verse18 Oh the depravity of my people! They don’t follow the rule of law and they don’t show any mercy. I’m only a man and I only have a man’s strength. I can no longer enforce my commands. VerseEnd Verse19 They’ve become strong in their perversion. They’re brutal as well, sparing no one, neither old nor young. And they take pleasure in everything except for what’s good. The suffering of our women and children throughout this land surpasses all. Indeed, words can’t describe it, and it can’t be written either. VerseEnd

Verse20 Now, my son, I won’t dwell any longer on this horrible scene. 2PSI You know this people’s wickedness, that they’re without principle and no longer capable of feeling, and their wickedness exceeds that of the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse21 I can’t recommend them to God, for fear He might strike me down. VerseEnd Verse22 But, my son, I recommend 2PSI you to God. And I trust in Christ that 2PSI you’ll be saved. I pray to God that He’ll spare 2PSI your life so 2PSI you can see in person either the return of His people to Him or their complete destruction. Because I know they will die unless they repent and return to Him. VerseEnd Verse23 If they die, it will be like the Jaredites, because of their determination to pursue blood and revenge. VerseEnd Verse24 If they die, we know many of our people have defected and joined the Lamanites, and many more will defect and join the Lamanites as well. So, write a few things if 2PSI you’re spared, in case I happen to die and don’t see 2PSI you. But I trust I can see 2PSI you soon since I have sacred records I wish to hand over to 2PSI you. VerseEnd

Verse25 My son, be faithful to Christ. Don’t allow what I’ve written to upset 2PSI you and weigh 2PSI you down to death, but allow Christ to lift 2PSI you up. May His suffering and death, and His appearance in person to our ancestors, and His mercy and long-suffering, and the hope of His glory and eternal life, rest in 2PP your mind forever. VerseEnd Verse26 And may the grace of God the Father — whose throne is high in the heavens — and of our Lord Jesus Christ — who sits on the right hand of His power until all things become subject to Him — may Their grace be with 2PP you and stay with 2PP you forever. Amen. VerseEnd
